abstract: Glutathione (GSH) supports diverse metabolic and antioxidant functions, yet the cellular processes most vulnerable to its depletion remain incompletely defined. Using genome-wide genetic screening in GSH depleted cells, we identified the cystine reductase TXNDC17 as essential for survival under GSH limitation. GSH depletion in TXNDC17-knockout cells caused intracellular cystine accumulation, increased protein cysteinylation, and cell death. Inhibiting the cystine/glutamate antiporter system xC- prevented cell death, linking this vulnerability to cystine uptake and impaired intracellular reduction. GSH depletion also markedly suppressed the growth of xenografts derived from TXNDC17-knockout, KEAP1-mutant lung cancer cells with high system xC- activity, accompanied by reduction-sensitive changes in cytoskeletal proteins. We further identified an electrophilic fragment that induced dose-dependent cytotoxicity in GSH-depleted cancer cells in a cystine-uptake dependent manner. Together, our findings establish TXNDC17 and GSH as central regulators of cystine-driven cytotoxicity, uncovering a therapeutic vulnerability in cancers with high cystine uptake.
